answer: A new identity enters after posting a time-locked work bond priced in saffron—costly enough that minting many names loses money—and finishing three staggered independently seeded micro-tasks. Each task is pressed as a signed receipt into an append-only shale; if two ledgers reuse a payment hop, a key-derivation prefix, or the same unlock schedule, both bonds burn. Countersigning neighbors keep a matching surety locked until the next close. The sureties interlock like a reef; when clustering later ties the newcomers together, the formation is slashed, so extra voters cost more than they return.
